answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation that accrues slowly and decays fast: an agent that wants to trade in the shared marketplace must first earn trust through small, verifiable jobs, like crossing a dune one careful step at a time rather than teleporting straight to the oasis. An identity that misbehaves loses its sable trust badge and the stake behind it, so spinning up a thousand fresh sock-puppets costs real work each time. Sybils stay cheap only when identities are free; make each one pay in proven history, and the attack stops scaling.
